meta.title: LUZ: a light, usable and zero-dependency design system for the web
meta.description: LUZ (Light, Usable & Zero-dependency) is a design system of tokens, CSS and a little vanilla JavaScript that starts from what the browser already does: native HTML, three color modes, one cascade layer you can always override, and no build step.

light.title: The light where you are
light.nojs: With JavaScript on, the light of your hour is drawn here.
light.fact.1: Light takes only 1.3 seconds to travel from the Moon to Earth.
light.fact.2: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach us; if the Sun went out, it would take us that long to notice.
light.fact.3: In just one second, a beam of light could travel around the Earth 7.5 times along the equator.
light.fact.4: A ‘light-year’ does not measure time, but the distance light travels in one year, which equals nearly 9.5 trillion kilometers.
light.fact.5: Due to the time light takes to travel, when you look at the stars at night you are seeing them as they were tens, hundreds, or thousands of years ago.
light.fact.6: According to current physics, the speed of light in a vacuum is the cosmic speed limit; nothing with mass can travel faster than it.
light.fact.7: Light slows down to about 225,000 km/s when traveling through water due to the density of the medium.
light.fact.8: In a laboratory, scientists managed to slow light down to just 61 kilometers per hour by passing it through extremely cold sodium.
light.fact.9: A light (or radio) signal takes between 3 and 22 minutes to reach Mars, depending on how aligned the planets are.
light.alt.globe: A globe lit by the sun as it is now, its land a puzzle with one faint grey piece for each country: the day side faces the light, the night side fades.

hero.title: LUZ Design system for humans, ready for AI.
hero.lead: Tokens, CSS and a little vanilla JavaScript, built on what the browser already does. Every component works before JavaScript loads, and every change starts with a failing test.
why.title: Three words, one promise.
why.lead: A CSS-first, zero-build design system for the web. Your CSS always wins, JavaScript is only an enhancement, and every page works before it loads.
why.weight.caption: The gzipped weight each package publishes, measured in dist when this page is built.
why.usable.sub: Accessible by default, not by add-on.
why.usable.caption: Counted when this page is built; what is short of 100% is in the statement.
why.usable.access: Built to WCAG 2.2 AA and EN 301 549, the EU standard for accessible digital products. It starts from what the browser does well, adds visible focus, contrast and reduced motion, and checks them with axe on every change. Read the statement.
why.zero.sub: Your code, not a tree of someone else’s.
why.zero.caption: Counted in every package’s package.json when this page is built.
why.light.text: Plain CSS and small ES modules, from a CDN or from npm. No preprocessor, no compiler and no build step: what you read in the files is exactly what the browser runs, and each package has a size ceiling that never goes up.
why.zero.text: LUZ’s packages ship with no dependencies: only CSS and ES modules over what the browser already offers. Nothing to install to try it, no framework to keep up with, and nothing that breaks when another library ships a new major version.

inside.l1.title: Your brand, as tokens
inside.l1.lead: Colors, scales and the three modes as CSS custom properties. No components: your markup, your classes.
inside.l1.p1.name: Colors.
inside.l1.p1.text: {n:primitives} primitives and {n:semantic} semantic tokens, in light, dark and high contrast.
inside.l1.p2.name: Scales.
inside.l1.p2.text: Space, type, radii and shadows, from three knobs.
inside.l2.title: Components with core
inside.l2.lead: Components and layout on top of the tokens, in one cascade layer your own CSS always beats.
inside.l2.p1.name: Components.
inside.l2.p1.text: {n:components} of them, from buttons and forms to tabs and a media player.
inside.l2.p2.name: Layout.
inside.l2.p2.text: {n:objects} objects for rows, grids, stacks and containers.
inside.l3.title: A whole site with the catalog
inside.l3.lead: What a site needs as a whole: search it, ask about cookies, switch its language.
inside.l3.p1.name: Search.
inside.l3.p1.text: A dialog on Ctrl K that, without JavaScript, is a link to the index.
inside.l3.p2.name: Language and notices.
inside.l3.p2.text: A language switch, submenus and a cookie notice that covers nothing.
inside.l4.title: Every site with its own template
inside.l4.lead: One package for each kind of site, on top of all the rest: install yours and it brings what it needs.
inside.l4.panel: The packages for each kind of site
inside.l4.p1.name: Four kinds.
inside.l4.p1.text: A landing page, a publication, an application and a documentation site.
inside.l4.p2.name: CSS only.
inside.l4.p2.text: None adds JavaScript: they are layout and style.

native.title: One tag, one class, zero JS
native.lead: Write the element you mean. Add LUZ's class. The browser does the rest.
native.p1.name: No script.
native.p1.text: {n:cssonly} of {n:components} components are CSS only: nothing to load.
native.p2.name: One class each.
native.p2.text: A component is a native element and one class: no wrappers, no utility chains.

native.p3.text: The other {n:withjs} improve with a script, and each page says what you get without it.
native.panel: Native elements, working with no script
modes.title: One interface, three modes
modes.lead: Every semantic color is defined for light, dark and high contrast. One attribute, data-theme, switches them: on the whole page, or on one part of it, like each box below.
modes.apply.light: Click to see the page in light mode
modes.apply.dark: Click to see the page in dark mode
modes.apply.contrast: Click to see the page in high contrast
modes.light.title: Light, for reading by day
modes.light.text: Warm paper and brown ink: Vejer's tone. It is the default: with no data-theme, the page looks like this.
modes.dark.title: Dark, for the night
modes.dark.text: Deep surfaces and light text that does not glare. The same tokens with other values: no component changes a line.
modes.contrast.title: High contrast, to see every edge
modes.contrast.text: Black on white and marked edges, for the reader who needs more. Not dark mode: a mode of its own, measured like the other two.
fit.good.public: Content sites, documentation and public services that must meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
fit.good.server: Server-rendered pages and static sites, in any back-end language.
fit.good.own: Teams that want to read and own their CSS.
fit.bad.react: You need ready-made React or Vue components.
fit.bad.grid: You need a data grid, charts or a date-range picker: LUZ has none.
fit.bad.beta: You need a stable API today: LUZ is in beta, and names can still change.
